status.en: 212 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 19% fewer than the week before, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Kaduna.
status.nb: 212 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 19 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen have continued high-profile attacks in northern Nigeria, killing civilians in Plateau and abducting residents from Kaduna's Millennium City estate. Bandits stormed a Kaduna estate again, taking six people, while soldiers repelled an assault in Benue and recovered rifles. A large-scale assault in the northeast resulted in at least 62 deaths. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpnede menn har fortsatt høyprofilerte angrep i Nord-Nigeria, drept sivile i Plateau og bortført innbyggere fra Millennium City-området i Kaduna. Banditter stormet et Kaduna-område igjen, og tok seks personer, mens soldater avverget et angrep i Benue og gjenvant rifler. Et omfattende angrep i nordøst resulterte i minst 62 dødsfall. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
